sites.title: Title
sites.hostnames_help: Comma separated, e.g. docs.example.org. Point these names to this server (DNS, reverse proxy, certificate).
sites.disable_help: The site is no longer served; its content and settings are kept.
sites.delete_confirm: Delete the site “{name}” with all its pages, files and settings? This cannot be undone.
sites.admins_help: Instance administrators manage the sites, user accounts, groups, roles, the license and installed plugins, and are administrators on every site. Administrators of the site main are instance administrators automatically.
sites.admin_unknown: Choose a user from the list.
sites.shared_notice: User accounts, groups and roles are shared by all sites of this instance. Here you assign roles for this site; instance administrators create and change accounts, groups and roles.
mail.ca_cert_help: Certificate of an internal certificate authority that signed the relay's certificate (PEM text or a file path) – safer than switching the check off.
sites.accounts_help: Shared: the users, groups and roles of the instance (rights per site). Own accounts: the site has its own users, groups and roles and does not see the others – for strictly separated groups of people. Cannot be changed later.
sites.first_admin_help: A site with own accounts starts without users: this local account becomes its administrator.
sites.first_admin_pw_help: Password rules of the site apply.
category.hidden_help: Not shown in the navigation, menus, listings and search – e.g. as a folder for media. Rights apply as usual.
media.library_help: Images, documents and other files of this site. Each file belongs to a category and has its rights; files can also get their own rights.
media.alt_help: Describes the image for people who cannot see it (screen readers). Leave empty only for decorative images.
media.category_help: The file gets the rights of this category (hidden categories work as folders).
media.crop_help: Drag a rectangle on the image or enter the values (pixels of the original).
media.delete_confirm: Delete "{name}"? Pages that show it will show nothing in its place.
media.download_help: Off: the file can only be viewed, also by people with all rights except managing it.
media.download_to_open: Download the file to open it.
media.no_steps: Add at least one step first.
media.not_viewable: This file can only be viewed in the browser if it is an image, a PDF, a video or audio file.
media.own_rights_help: Replaces the rights of the category and of the pages that show the file. You can only give rights you have yourself.
media.type.label: Type
media.unused: Not used on any page you can see.
media.wm.title: Watermark
media.wm.help: Burnt into images and PDFs. With the viewer's name, every person sees their own name – copies can be traced.
media.wm.uploader_only: Do not keep the original – only the version with the uploader's watermark
media.wm.uploader_view: Show with the uploader's watermark, original for downloads
media.wm.viewer_view: Burn in the viewer's name when shown
media.wm.viewer_all: Burn in the viewer's name when shown and downloaded
media.wm.uploader_only_warn: The original file is not stored and cannot be restored later.
gallery.title: Image
macro.template_help: Only templates for all pages or for this space can be used by everybody; a personal template shows the button to you alone.
office.editing: Editing – changes are saved as a new version
office.read_only_protected: Read-only, without download, print and copy
office.no_renderer: The browser part of this office program is missing (plugin active?).
office.not_configured: Not set up yet: enter the server address and save.
settings.viewer_help: Office files open in this program; what it cannot open, the browser shows. The details of a file offer further programs.
settings.open_external: Always open files directly in the default program
settings.open_external_help: A click on a suitable file opens it there right away instead of the details. Only possible for the default program.
settings.office_token_ttl_help: How long an opened document can be saved (default 10h, at most 24h). Rights are checked again on every access.
office.using: Connected via {url} (empty field: preset from the environment, e.g. Docker Compose).
demo.title: Demo content
demo.help: Creates an area “Demo: Enterprise Wiki” with one click. It shows as many features as possible: pages with blocks, Markdown, blog, FAQ, calendar with series and registration, team page, media with gallery and watermark, files, workflow. Also page properties, comments, reactions, menu, text block and carousel. The demo accounts of the team page cannot sign in and do not count for the license. “Remove demo” deletes everything the demo created without a trace – including versions, trash, files and log entries. Your own content stays untouched.
demo.created_without: Demo created, without these parts (a plugin is switched off or a permission is missing): {parts}
demo.remove_confirm: Everything the demo created is deleted permanently, including your changes to demo content. Continue?
demo.reset_title: Reset the site to its first start
demo.reset_help: Deletes all content, media, files, versions, the trash, the log and the settings of this site. Only your administrator account and the welcome page remain – as at the first start. Address, languages, e-mail delivery, site name and license stay. On an instance with several sites and shared accounts the accounts stay.
demo.reset_warning: Caution: this cannot be undone. Make a backup first.
demo.reset_confirm: To confirm, type the name of the site: {name}
demo.reset_last: Really delete everything? You sign in again afterwards.
editor.heading: Heading {level}
editor.link_invalid: Only http(s), mailto, /path and #anchor links are allowed.
editor.image_alt_help: Describe the image for people who cannot see it.
editor.macro_none: No blocks are available (no block plugin is active).
editor.html_help: HTML that Markdown cannot express (e.g. merged table cells). It is sanitized when saved; leave it empty to remove it.
editor.help_visual: Alt+F10: toolbar · Esc then Tab: leave the editor · Enter on a block or image: edit it · Markdown like **bold** or # heading is converted while typing.
editor.help_markdown: Markdown source (GitHub Flavored Markdown). Blocks: ::name{key=value} or :::name … ::: with content.
profile.editor_help: Both editors save Markdown; you can switch at any time.
scheme.label: Colour scheme
scheme.light_only: This template has light colours only.
scheme.help: “Same as system” follows the setting of your device. Applies to every template with light and dark colours.
settings.editor_help: Users can choose their own editor in their profile.
editor.live_alone: Live editing: nobody else is editing this page right now.
editor.live_joined: {name} is now editing this page too.
editor.live_lost: The connection for live editing ended. You keep editing alone; changes of others are no longer shown.
editor.live_unavailable: Live editing is not available right now. You are editing alone.
editor.live_saved: Revision {rev} was saved by another editor. Your next save builds on it.
editor.live_saved_by: {name} saved revision {rev}. Your next save builds on it.
settings.collaboration: Live editing (several editors at the same time)
settings.collaboration_help: Editors of a page see each other's changes and cursors, in the visual editor and in the Markdown source.
editor.live_replaced: Others were already editing this page: what you typed before the connection was replaced by the shared state.
editor.mode_shared: Switches the view for everybody who is editing now.
email.confirm_text:
Hello {name},

please confirm that {email} is your address by opening this link (valid for {hours} hours):

{link}

If you did not add this address, ignore this message; nothing changes.
email.title: E-mail addresses
email.help: Notifications go to the primary address. Every confirmed address identifies you: you can sign in with it, and sign-ins of other providers with that address are linked to your account.
email.sent: A confirmation link was sent to {email}.
email.add_help: You get a link to confirm that the address is yours.
email.confirm_now_help: Only if you know that the address belongs to this person.
identity.title: Sign-ins
identity.help: Ways to sign in to this account. Further sign-ins are added when you sign in with another method using one of your confirmed addresses.
identity.unlink_confirm: Remove the sign-in {provider} ({name}) from this account?
identity.link_intro: You signed in with {provider} as {name}. The address {email} belongs to an existing account.
identity.link_how: Sign in with that account once to link the two – afterwards both lead to the same account.
identity.linked: {provider} is now linked to your account.
invite.title: Invite
invite.help: Creates the account for an e-mail address in advance. The person gets it, with these groups and roles, at the first sign-in with a trusted single sign-on that confirms the address.
session.title: Sessions
session.help: You are signed in here. End sessions you do not recognise, then change your password. Changing your password ends all other sessions.
session.end_confirm: End the session “{device}”? Signing in again will be required there.
session.end_others_confirm: End all other sessions? This session stays signed in.
session.end_all_confirm: End all sessions of this user?
mapping.jit: Create accounts at the first sign-in (JIT)
mapping.jit_help: Off: only people created or invited in advance and already linked sign-ins get in.
mapping.trust_email_help: A new sign-in with an address the provider confirms is linked to the account with that address automatically. Only for providers that check addresses reliably.
mapping.email_verified: The provider confirms all e-mail addresses
mapping.email_verified_help: For LDAP and SAML whose addresses come from a maintained directory. OpenID Connect tells this itself (claim email_verified).
authadmin.instance_help: Several providers of the same kind are possible (e.g. two OpenID Connect providers), each with its own settings, mapping and JIT rules.
authadmin.add_help: The id becomes part of the addresses and of user handles (name@provider). Do not change it once people have signed in with it.
authadmin.id_help: 1–24 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Provider id: {base}-<id>.
authadmin.id_invalid: The id may only contain lower-case letters, digits and hyphens (at most 24 characters).
authadmin.name: Name on the login page
authadmin.added: Provider “{name}” added. Now complete its settings.
authadmin.remove_confirm: Remove the provider “{id}”? People who only sign in with it cannot sign in any more.
authadmin.preview_help: Shows what a sign-in with these details would lead to: account, groups and roles. Nothing is stored. Uses the saved settings.
authadmin.outcome.existing: Signs in to the existing account {user}
authadmin.outcome.link_confirm: The address belongs to {user}: the person confirms the link with their previous sign-in
authadmin.outcome.refused: Refused: no account and JIT is off
scim.help: Directories such as Microsoft Entra ID or Okta manage people and groups through SCIM 2.0: create, change, disable and remove. This works even before anybody signs in. A client may only manage people of its sign-in and groups it created, never administrators and never roles. Which roles a provisioned group gets is up to you (Groups).
scim.add_help: You then get the tenant URL and the token for the directory. The token is shown only once.
scim.name: Name
scim.provider_help: The provisioned people sign in with this. Their account is recognised then.
scim.subject_from_help: Which SCIM attribute is the stable id at the provider. Entra ID with OpenID Connect: externalId (objectId), and claim_subject: oid at the provider.
scim.renew_confirm: Create a new token for “{name}”? The current one stops working.
scim.delete_confirm: Delete the SCIM client “{name}”? The provisioned people and groups stay.
scim.token_once: Copy the token into the directory now. It is not shown again.
scim.no_provider: First set up a sign-in method (e.g. OpenID Connect).
mfa.none: No usable factor is available for this account. Please contact the administration.
mfa.by_provider: Further factors of your sign-in are handled by your sign-in provider (identity provider).
auth.passkey_cancelled: The sign-in with a passkey was cancelled.
photo.vis.label: Who sees my photo?
photo.vis.help: Without a photo the wiki shows your initials.
settings.session_idle_help: e.g. 12h or 30m; 0 = only the validity above. Automatic requests do not count as activity.
settings.photo_default_help: For people who did not choose.
settings.photo_max_help: Nobody can share their photo more widely. More narrowly is always possible.
settings.photo_fixed_help: All photos are then visible exactly as the default says.
perm.core.photos.view_help: See every profile photo, also those their owners show to nobody (e.g. for identity checks).
alias.label: User name (optional)
alias.help: Unique name in the wiki; signing in with it is possible too.
alias.help_self: Unique name in the wiki. You can sign in with it as well.
alias.managed: Comes from the sign-in method {provider} and is set again at the next sign-in.
alias.managed_self: Comes from your sign-in method and cannot be changed here.
mapping.username_from_help: Attribute, claim or SAML attribute that becomes the user name in the wiki (e.g. uid, cn, preferred_username). Updated at every sign-in; if the name is taken, the previous one stays.
mfa.title: Sign-in factors
mfa.chain_help: Your sign-in asks the factors in this order; factors with the same number are alternatives. A sign-in needs {required} factor(s).
mfa.choose_setup: What do you want to set up?
mfa.enroll_help: This sign-in needs {required} factors; you have {passed}. Please set up another factor now.
admin.reset_mfa_help: Removes authenticator app, codes by e-mail and security keys of this user; they are set up again at the next sign-in if it needs them.
mfa.admin.help: Every MFA plugin is a factor of the sign-in. Factors with the same number are alternatives; higher numbers are asked afterwards. Factor 1 (only plugins that sign in without password, e.g. passkeys) is an alternative to the password.
mfa.admin.factors_help: The number decides when the factor is asked (1 to 9).
mfa.admin.factor_help: 2 = second factor (default); 3 and more for a longer chain.
mfa.admin.factor_help_first: 1 = instead of the password (default for passkeys); 2 or more = additional factor.
mfa.admin.factor_invalid: Please enter a whole number from {min} to 9.
mfa.admin.enable_help: As which factor should it be asked? Factors with the same number are alternatives.
mfa.admin.providers_help: Which factors apply to the people of each sign-in method (instance), and how many factors a sign-in needs. Who has fewer sets one up during the sign-in.
mfa.admin.required_help: 1 = the first factor is enough (further factors only for people who set them up); 2 = at least one further factor, and so on.
mfa.admin.counts_two_help: The device checks the person itself (PIN, fingerprint, face): the passkey also covers the following factor of the chain.
sources.help: Elements of the sources are shown together, each once, and only to readers who may see them. Without a source: this category with its subcategories.
category.template_help: Look of this category and its subcategories – e.g. the CMS template for a public area. Without an own choice the template of the parent category or of the site applies.
space.help: Every top-level category is a space. These settings apply to the whole space with all subcategories. Everybody with the permission Manage here may change them – without administrator rights.
space.key_help: 2–16 letters and digits, starting with a letter (e.g. HR). Short address: {origin}/s/KEY. Leave empty for no key.
space.own_tree_help: Inside the space the sidebar shows only its categories and shortcuts instead of the whole wiki.
space.shortcuts_help: Important pages or external addresses, at the top of the space navigation. Wiki paths (/…) or http(s) addresses; the label is for the current language.
space.allowed_types_help: Only these types can be created in the space or moved here. None selected: all active types.
space.language_help: New pages in the space are created in this language unless another is chosen.
space.directory_help: The spaces of the wiki you may see.
archive.title: Archive
archive.help: Archived categories and everything below them are read-only for everybody, administrators too. They no longer appear in navigation, overviews and search. You can restore them at any time. Direct links keep working.
archive.restore_help: This category is archived: read-only, not in navigation and search. Restoring makes it editable again.
archive.above: A parent category is archived, so this category is read-only. Restore it in the archived category.
archive.confirm: Archive the category with all subcategories and pages? Everything becomes read-only and leaves navigation and search; you can restore it at any time.
archive.notice: This content is read-only and does not appear in navigation and search.
template.scope_category: Everybody in this category and below
space.is_template: Offer as template for new spaces
space.is_template_help: New spaces can then be created with the structure, permissions, settings, website template and page templates of this space.
space.from_template_help: Takes over subcategories, permissions, settings, website template and page templates of the chosen space.
space.with_pages_help: Otherwise only the structure without pages.
space.import_help: Create a new space from a package made with “Export” (JSON Lines): categories, pages in all languages, settings and page templates. Permissions and files are not included; all content is checked like when saved.
space.import_below_help: Create a package made with “Export” (JSON Lines) as subcategory here. Permissions and files are not included; all content is checked like when saved.
space.io_help: Exports the space with all subcategories, pages (latest version of every language), settings and page templates as a file (JSON Lines) – e.g. to move it into another wiki. Permissions and files are not included.
access.help: The people who manage this area are notified if the content exists. You get a message as soon as they decide.
notify.access_request_help: Somebody asks for access to an area you manage.
notify.access_answer_help: Your request was granted or declined.
space.mine_help: Spaces where you, one of your groups or roles have permissions.
perm.core.spaces.personal_help: Create one own space (top-level category) that only its owner sees until they share it.
class.label: Classification
class.help: Applies to the category and everything below; the strictest classification above always applies. Internal: never for guests. Confidential: also not in feeds and calendar subscriptions, e-mails with title and link only, notice on every page. Strictly confidential: also not in the general search, no export and no copies.
class.notice.2: do not pass on; not in feeds and e-mails.
class.notice.3: for authorized people only; not in search, exports, copies, feeds and e-mails.
insights.help: Views are counted per page and day only – without people or addresses – and deleted after 400 days. The subcategories you may see are included.
insights.stale: Not changed for more than 6 months
space.allowed_macros_help: Only these blocks are offered and shown in the space (others appear as a notice). None selected: all active blocks.
space.logo_help: Picture of the wiki (upload or address /api/v1/files/… or /api/v1/media/…); shown in the navigation and the directory.
space.accent_help: Color of links and buttons in the space. It needs a contrast of at least 4.5:1 with white (WCAG); too light colors are refused.
protect.wm_auto: Automatic: from “Confidential” with name and time
protect.wm_help: Applies to pictures and PDFs of the media library and pictures in pages of this category and below (the nearest setting above counts).
protect.dl_help: Applies to media and file elements. With the permission to manage, downloading is always possible.
sources.zone_help.include: Click a building block or drag it here.
sources.zone_help.exclude: Elements matching one of these are never shown.
sources.zone_help.require: Only elements that also match each of these.
settings.lists_max_help: Upper bound for lists from sources (blocks, blog, FAQ …) and for search and filter sources: 0 = 1000, at most 10000. Editors choose their limit and pages below it.
limits.intro: The technical limits of the wiki and all plugins in one place. Each value has a default and an allowed range. Changes apply at once unless noted and are recorded in the audit log.
limits.instance_only: The limits apply to the whole instance. Only its administrators change them.
limits.out_of_range: Please enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
wait.title: The server has not answered yet
wait.text: The change is on its way but not confirmed yet. What you entered is kept whatever you choose.
wait.cancelled: Cancelled. What you entered is still here; reload to see whether the change was already stored.
error.too_large: The request is too large. The administration sets the limit (expert settings).
error.busy: The server is busy right now. Nothing was stored; please try again in a moment.
limit.core.request.guest_kb.help: Largest body of a request that carries no session and no API key (sign-in, forms of guests).
limit.core.request.body_kb.help: Largest body of a request of a signed-in user. Routes that need more declare their own limit.
limit.core.request.content_kb.help: Largest body when saving pages, drafts, templates and previews.
limit.core.request.sso_kb.help: Largest SAML or OIDC message and SCIM request.
limit.core.request.import_mb.help: Largest file when importing categories or translations.
limit.core.request.large_parallel: Large requests at the same time
limit.core.request.large_parallel.help: How many requests larger than 1 MB are processed at once (uploads are streamed and do not count). Further ones wait.
limit.core.request.large_wait_s.help: How long a large request waits for a free place before it is answered with "busy" (503). Nothing is stored in that case; the sender repeats it.
limit.core.audit.value_guest_bytes.help: Longest value in the audit log for events without a signed-in user (e.g. failed sign-ins). Longer values are shortened; the original length is noted.
limit.core.audit.value_bytes.help: Longest before/after value in the audit log for events of signed-in users.
limit.core.ui.wait_notice_s.help: After this time without an answer to a change the user is asked whether to keep waiting or to cancel. The entered content is kept in both cases.
limit.core.rate.user_per_second.help: Requests per second a signed-in account may send in the long run. Beyond it the answer is 429 with the time to wait.
limit.core.rate.user_burst.help: Requests an account may send at once before the rate per second applies (opening a page sends several).
limit.core.rate.guest_per_second: Requests of an address without sign-in
limit.core.rate.guest_per_second.help: Requests per second of all guests behind one address. Behind a reverse proxy the address of the client counts (server.trusted_proxies).
limit.core.rate.guest_burst: Reserve of an address without sign-in
limit.core.rate.guest_burst.help: Requests an address may send at once before the rate per second applies.
limit.core.rate.expensive_per_second.hel: Searches, previews, exports and uploads per second of an account or address, on top of the general limit.
limit.core.rate.expensive_burst.help: Expensive requests an account or address may send at once.
limit.core.live.persons.help: How many persons edit one page together at the same time. Further ones see the page and are told that it is full.
limit.core.live.connections_per_person.h: How many windows or devices of one person edit the same page at once.
limit.core.audit.search_days.help: How far back the text search in before/after values of the audit log looks when no start date is given. With a start date any period is searched.
limit.core.watch.quiet_seconds.help: How long an immediate watch notification waits after the last change. So several saves in a row become one e-mail.
limit.core.placements.rows.help: How many placements of building blocks one level (template, site, category, instance or person) may have.
limit.core.elements.rules.help: How many own permission rules one page (element) may have.
limit.core.rollback.structure_changes.he: Most moves and orders since the chosen point in time that one rollback of a category with its structure undoes; more are refused (choose a later point in time).
limit.core.rollback.structure_changes: Changes undone by a rollback of the structure
limits.proxy.title: Address of visitors
limits.proxy.info: Behind a reverse proxy the address of visitors comes from the header {header} – only from the {n} configured proxies (server.trusted_proxies). The header is chosen with server.client_ip_header.
limits.proxy.none: No reverse proxy is configured (server.trusted_proxies): the address of the direct connection counts.
limits.proxy.warning: These addresses send the header {header} but are not configured as proxies. The header is ignored: all visitors behind them share one address (request limits, sign-in protection, audit log). If it is your reverse proxy, add it to server.trusted_proxies.
limits.keys.title: API keys
limits.keys.help: Own limit per key in requests per second. Empty: the limit of the account applies. A limit granted here is a budget of the key itself and may exceed the limit of the account (integrations).
limits.keys.none: There are no valid API keys.
limits.keys.name: Key
apikey.rate_help: Limits this key below the limit of your account. Higher limits are granted by the administration.
secrets.title: Secrets in the database
secrets.mode.plain: Mode: plain – signing keys and secrets of authenticator apps are protected by the access to the database.
secrets.mode.aes: Mode: aes – encrypted with AES-256-GCM and the key file of the instance.
secrets.mode.pq: Mode: pq – encrypted post-quantum (ML-KEM-1024 + X25519, AES-256-GCM) with the key file of the instance.
secrets.key_password: The key file is loaded and protected by a password.
secrets.rewrap_needed: Some values are not stored in the current mode yet.
secrets.help: The mode is set in config.yaml (secrets.mode: plain, aes or pq); a key file is created at the first start (secrets.key next to config.yaml). Optionally the variable {env} protects the key file with a password. Then store all values in the new mode.
secrets.rewrap: Store all values in the current mode
webhook.text.user.enabled: The account of {title} ({username}) is active again.
webhook.text.group.member_removed: {title} ({username}) is no longer in the group {group_name}.
webhooks.accounts_in_all: Also send changes of accounts to webhooks with all events
webhooks.accounts_in_all_help: Changes of accounts (people created, deactivated, deleted, group memberships) contain personal data. Off (recommended): only webhooks that chose these events get them.
signature.unsupported: This way of signing is not available in this browser.
signature.title: Signature
signature.valid: The signature is valid: the record is unchanged, the signature of the person and the seal of the wiki verify.
signature.invalid: The signature is NOT valid – see the checks below.
signature.check.seal.key_of_this_wiki: Seal key belongs to this wiki
signature.export_help: The export contains everything needed to verify the signature elsewhere, e.g. with: ewiki signature verify FILE.
signature.verify_help: Choose an exported signature (JSON). The wiki checks the record, the signature of the person and its seal, and whether the seal key is one of this wiki.
signature.verify_too_big: The file is too big for a signature.
signature.verify_not_json: The file is not an exported signature (JSON).
signature.keys_help: Compare the fingerprint in an export with these to know that a signature comes from this wiki.
error.reauth_required: Please sign in again. This change is only possible within 15 minutes of signing in.
plugins.origin.level_help.official: This core plugin comes from the Enterprise Wiki project.
plugins.origin.level_help.organisation: This source is entered as trusted.
plugins.origin.level_help.external: This source is neither official nor entered as trusted.
plugins.origin.level_help.unknown: It is not known where this core plugin comes from.
plugins.origin.core_warning: Core plugins run inside the wiki process and have the same rights as the wiki itself: they can read and change all data. Only install code you trust.
plugins.origin.external_warning: Warning: this source is not known as trusted in your organisation. Foreign code can steal data, bypass rights or damage the wiki. Review the code first or ask the people responsible for security.
plugins.origin.accept_label: I have read the warning and install this core plugin anyway.
plugins.origin.accept_required: Please confirm the warning with the checkbox.
plugins.origin.external_forbidden: Core plugins from external sources are switched off in this wiki. Enter the source as trusted or allow external sources.
plugins.sources.title: Trusted sources
plugins.sources.help: Core plugins from these sources count as plugins of your organisation and need no extra confirmation. An entry covers the address and everything below it. Adding entries and allowing external sources needs a sign-in within the last 15 minutes.
plugins.sources.prefix_help: e.g. https://git.example.com/team or /srv/plugins. Only https and ssh, at least one path segment.
plugins.sources.remove_confirm: Remove source {prefix}? Core plugins already installed stay installed.
plugins.sources.allow_external: Allow core plugins from external sources (with warning and confirmation)
plugins.sources.allow_external_help: Switched off, only official core plugins and those from trusted sources can be installed.
plugins.credentials.title: Access data for plugin sources
plugins.credentials.help: For plugins from private repositories: the wiki sends the token only to addresses below the prefix, over https, when installing, updating and checking for updates. It is never shown again after saving.
plugins.credentials.prefix_help: https address the repositories lie below, e.g. https://github.com/acme or https://git.example.com/team. An entry with the same prefix is replaced.
plugins.credentials.token_help: Preferably a read-only token for the repositories needed only. References to environment variables are possible in config.yaml only.
limit.core.auth.passkey_autofill_per_5mi: Passkey offers on the sign-in page

Passkey requests of the user name field per address in 5 minutes. Every view of the sign-in page starts one. Many people behind one address (company network) need a high value. A request alone signs nobody in.
login_admin.title: Sign-in page
login_admin.help: These settings apply at once and are saved apart from the other settings.
login_admin.autofill: Suggest passkeys in the “User name” field
login_admin.autofill_help: The browser shows saved passkeys among the suggestions of the field. Only when the person picks one does it ask for fingerprint, face or PIN. The button “Sign in with a passkey” always stays. Switch this off if assistive technology (for example a screen reader) has problems with the suggestions.
login_admin.auto_help: The sign-in page sends everyone straight to this provider. Not after errors, after signing out and while confirming further factors. Emergency access for admins: /login?local=1
login_admin.no_buttons: There is no provider with its own sign-in page yet (for example OpenID Connect or SAML). Providers like LDAP need no button: they check user name and password in the form.
login_admin.order_help: Lower numbers come first (−1000 to 1000). Same number: by name.
login_admin.label: Text of the button
login_admin.label_help: Empty: the name of the provider. At most 80 characters.
login_admin.shown: Show the button on the sign-in page
login_admin.shown_help: Without a button the provider can only be reached with the direct link.
register.title: Create an account at {site}
register.intro: You will get an e-mail with a link. Your account is created only when you open this link.
register.closed: Accounts cannot be created here. Please contact the administrators.
register.name: Name
register.email_help: You will sign in with this address.
register.password_help: Choose a long password that you do not use anywhere else.
register.password_mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
register.sent: We sent an e-mail to {email}. Open the link in it within {hours} hours to create your account.
register.sent_spam: No e-mail? Look in your spam folder. If the address already has an account, the e-mail says so.
register.have_account: Already have an account? Sign in
register.created: Your account for {email} is created. You can sign in now.
email.register_text:
Hello {name},

please open this link to create your account at {site} for {email} (valid for {hours} hours):

{link}

If you did not ask for an account, ignore this message. Without the link no account is created.
email.register_exists_text:
Hello,

somebody tried to create a new account at {site} for {email}. This address already belongs to an account. Sign in with it:

{login}

If you forgot your password, use “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page (if offered) or contact the administrators. If this was not you, ignore this message; nothing changes.
login_admin.reg_enabled: People may create a local account themselves
login_admin.reg_enabled_help: The sign-in page shows “Create an account”. The account is created only when the person opens the link in the e-mail. The answer never tells whether an address already has an account.
login_admin.reg_not_here: This site uses the accounts of the main site. Switch registration on there.
login_admin.reg_no_mail: Sending e-mail is not set up. Without e-mail, registration is not available.
login_admin.reg_domains_help: Separated by commas, for example example.com or *.example.com for all subdomains. Empty: any address.
login_admin.reg_groups_help: Groups with an administrator role cannot be chosen here.
limit.core.auth.register_per_hour.help: Requests for a new local account per address in one hour (only when registration is switched on).
limit.core.auth.registrations_pending.he: Registrations waiting for their confirmation link at the same time. Beyond it new registrations wait; unconfirmed ones expire after 48 hours.
reset.title: Forgot your password
reset.intro: Enter the e-mail address of your account. You will get a link to set a new password.
reset.closed: Resetting the password is not available here. Please contact the administrators.
reset.email_help: A confirmed address of your account.
reset.sent: If {email} belongs to an account, we sent an e-mail. The link in it is valid for {minutes} minutes.
reset.sent_hint: No e-mail? Look in your spam folder or check the address.
reset.new_intro: Afterwards you are signed out everywhere and sign in with the new password. Further factors (for example a passkey) still apply.
reset.done: Your new password is saved. You can sign in now.
email.password_reset_text:
Hello {name},

use this link to set a new password for your account at {site} (valid for {minutes} minutes, once):

{link}

If you did not ask for this, ignore this message; your password stays the same.
email.password_reset_external_text:
Hello {name},

somebody asked for a new password for {email} at {site}. Your account has no password of its own in the wiki: you sign in through {provider}. Change the password there or ask your IT.

Sign in: {login}

If this was not you, ignore this message; nothing changes.
login_admin.reset_help: People with a local account get a link by e-mail (valid for 1 hour). The answer never tells whether an address has an account. Switch this off if only the administrators should reset passwords.
login_admin.reset_no_mail: Sending e-mail is not set up. Without e-mail, “Forgot your password?” and registration are not available.
Requests of “Forgot your password?” per sender address in one hour.
perm.core.users.list_all_help: Find every active user by name, e.g. in permission and share dialogs.
perm.core.users.list_own: List users of the own groups
perm.core.users.list_own_help: Find the users who share a group with oneself.
perm.core.groups.list_all_help: See the names of all groups, e.g. in permission and share dialogs.
perm.core.groups.list_own_help: See the names of the groups one belongs to.
perm.core.roles.list_all_help: See the names of all roles, e.g. in permission and share dialogs.
perm.core.roles.list_own_help: See the names of the roles one has (directly or through a group).
audit.action.settings.config_set: Setting changed on the command line
audit.action.settings.file_changed: Configuration file changed outside the wiki
block.core.element.title: Title of the page
placement.help_instance: Where the title, buttons and sections of this page appear. Blocks you do not change keep the placement of the category and the site (inherited).
editor_tools.help: Which buttons the formatting toolbar shows when editing. Hidden formatting stays possible with shortcuts and Markdown. The switch to Markdown always stays. Where the toolbar is, or whether it is shown at all, is set in the placement.
editor_tools.none: Choose at least one button. For no toolbar, hide it in the placement.
settings.custom_css_help: People who may design templates can add own CSS to a template of data. It is checked on saving (no @import, url() only to files of the wiki, nothing that runs). Own CSS can make the wiki less accessible; switched off, own CSS of templates is no longer used.
settings.personal_placement_help: Signed-in people arrange the building blocks of the interface for themselves under “My profile → My arrangement”. Required blocks stay where they are.
dashboard.title: My dashboard
dashboard.help: Your tiles at a glance. Arrange them with the mouse (Move with the mouse) or with the keyboard (Arrange tiles).
dashboard.empty: No tiles yet. Add some with “Arrange tiles”.
dashboard.arrange_title: Arrange the tiles of my dashboard
dashboard.drag_on: Moving with the mouse is on: drag a tile to another place.
dashboard.drag_off: Moving with the mouse is off.
dashboard.none_mine: You have not edited any page yet.
dashboard.none_watches: You do not watch any page yet.
dashboard.offered_help: Which tiles everybody may put on the own dashboard. Where the tiles are by default, and which are required, is set above at the positions “Dashboard: column …”.
settings.dashboard_home: Own dashboard as the start page
settings.dashboard_home_help: Signed-in people see their own dashboard after signing in and at “/”. The start page of the wiki stays at “/start”. Guests still see the start page.
dashboard.site_home: Go to the start page of the wiki
block.core.category.title: Category: title
category.arrange_help: Applies to this category only, not to its subcategories. Here you also choose which pages are shown in full (featured pages) and where.
display.title: Display of the pages
display.help: How the category page shows its pages. The choice also applies to the subcategories until one of them chooses its own.
display.view_help: Handbook: the pages are a navigation in the side column, also on every page of the category.
display.sort.title: by title
display.page_size_help: Empty: as many as the expert setting allows. Beyond that the list is paged.
display.subcategories: Also the pages of the subcategories
display.excerpt: Show the beginning of the text
limit.core.categories.page_size: Pages per page of a category overview
limit.core.categories.page_size.help: How many pages the overview of a category shows at most at once; more are paged. A category may choose fewer.
limit.core.categories.featured.help: How many pages a category page shows in full (featured pages) at most.
display.columns_help: For example properties of the pages. Everybody sees only values they may see.
display.columns_none: There are no further columns here yet.
category.not_loaded: This page could not be loaded.
limit.core.content.includes_per_page.hel: How many pages one page may show with the block "Include page", counted over all levels. Further ones show a note.
limit.core.categories.full: Whole pages per page of a category overview
limit.core.categories.full.help: How many pages the views accordion, tabs and all one below the other show in full at once; more are paged.
bo.changed: The options of {block} were changed. Save to use them.
bo.cleared: The options of {block} were removed. Save to use that.
bo.title: Options: {block}
bo.help: How the block looks and when it is shown, at this position. Empty fields keep the default. Showing it only to some is a rule of display, not a permission.
bo.anchor_help: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Links to #name jump here.
bo.problems: {n} problem(s): the options cannot be used like this.
bo.sample_text: This sample text shows how text, colours and spacing look with these options.
bo.group.general.help: Where, when and for whom the block is shown, and how it prints.
bo.group.size.help: Values per view: the tablet takes the desktop value, the phone the tablet value, unless they have their own.
bo.group.background.help: A background of its own needs a text colour of its own; its contrast is checked. Text on a picture needs an overlay.
bo.group.text.help: Columns get narrower down to 12 rem; where they do not fit, there are fewer.
bo.break_before: New page before it when printing
bo.bg_video: Background video (silent, with a pause button)
bo.p.form: Some values do not have a valid form.
bo.p.text_color: A block with its own background needs its own text colour, so its contrast can be checked.
bo.p.gradient: A gradient needs its two colours.
bo.p.overlay: Text on a picture needs an overlay, so it can be read on every part of the picture.
bo.p.gradient_text_bg: Headings in the gradient need a background colour of their own.
bo.p.contrast: {color} has a contrast of {value}:1 on {on}; at least {min}:1 is needed.
bo.p.columns: On the {view} at most {max} column(s) of text have room side by side; set fewer for this view.
bo.sample_wait: The sample shows the options once there is no problem left.
bo.p.between: The text colour {color} lies within the brightness of its background ({from} to {to}); choose a much lighter or darker text colour or a stronger overlay.
icon.found_more: {n} icons, the first {shown} are shown; search more precisely to see others.
editor.leave_text: This page has changes that are not saved yet. What would you like to do?
editor.leave_draft: Save as draft and go on
draft.preview_note_drafted: Preview – this is how the page will look when published. Your changes are saved as a draft, but not published yet.
draft.preview_links: Links open in a new tab.
editor.parts_help: In the editor the block starts with two parts ({part}). Add more with “+ {part}” at the top of the block.
editor.parts_help_titled: In the editor the block starts with two parts ({part}): the heading is the title, the content goes below it. Add more with “+ {part}” at the top of the block.
error.foreign: This answer did not come from the wiki ({what}) but from a service in front of it. This is for example a proxy or a web application firewall. Answer: “{body}”. Please tell the administration. For administrators: the section “Behind a web application firewall” of the installation guide lists the exclusions needed.
layout.embed_remember: Always load content from {host} in this browser
layout.embed_forgotten: From the next visit on, content from {host} loads only after you agree.
settings.embed_allow: Services allowed for external videos and embeds
settings.embed_allow_help: One address per line, only https:// and the server (for example https://www.youtube-nocookie.com or https://player.vimeo.com). Empty: nothing from outside the wiki is embedded. Content loads only after the reader agrees.
placement.scope_pages: On all pages of the category
placement.scope_pages_on: {block} is now also on all pages of the category.
placement.scope_pages_off: {block} is now only on the page of the category itself.
placement.scope_sub_on: {block} now also applies in the subcategories.
placement.scope_sub_off: {block} no longer applies in the subcategories.
editor.block_keys: Arrow keys: through the groups; arrow right opens a group, arrow left closes it; Enter: insert.
profile.help_texts_help: Explanations of fields and settings. Notes you need to fill in a field correctly are always there. The “?” button at the top switches the same.
diagram.title: Diagram
diagram.error: The diagram could not be drawn. Its text is below.
editor.emoji_help: A word of the name or a keyword, for example “thumb” or “heart”. Arrow keys choose, Enter inserts.
editor.block_share: Save the selection as a shared block
editor.block_share_help: The selection becomes a block of its own (an element of the type Block in this category) and is included here. Include it on other pages with Include page; a change of the block shows everywhere. The block is changed on its own page.
data.intro: Blocks and plugins keep data for reports here, for example the decisions on pages. Reports show only entries of pages the reader may see. After a new plugin or a new version, the wiki builds the data from the latest versions of the pages; you can also start this again yourself.
data.rebuild_started: The data is being built again.
data.shown: {n} of {total} shown (only what you may see).
data.no_kinds: No kinds of data: no active plugin keeps data for reports.
bo.group.motion.help: The block appears while it is scrolled into view. Nothing moves for people who want less motion, nor in browsers that cannot tie the motion to scrolling; there the block is simply shown.
bo.appear.slide_start: Slide in from the start of the line
bo.appear.slide_end: Slide in from the end of the line
settings.not_found_page: Page with the text for “Page not found”
settings.forbidden_page: Page with the text for “No permission”
settings.error_page_help: The content of this page appears below the heading instead of the standard text; suggestions and the link to the start page stay. Readers see it only if they may see the page: choose a page everybody may see.
maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.intro: While the wiki is in maintenance, administrators keep working; everybody else can only read it (read-only) or sees only this message (closed). Signing in always works. Read-only suits moving the server: the wiki stays available, but nothing changes any more.
maintenance.mode_read_only: Read-only – everybody can read, only administrators can change things
maintenance.mode_closed: Closed – only administrators can use the wiki
maintenance.mode_help: The server refuses every change by others (pages, files, comments, settings, live editing, SCIM, documents of office programs); the interface says why.
maintenance.message_help: Plain text; an empty line starts a new paragraph. Empty: a standard text.
maintenance.until_help: Only shown; the mode does not end by itself.
maintenance.run_jobs_help: By default they wait (sending e-mails, clean-up, retention, building data …), so the database does not change; a copy taken now sends no e-mail twice. Running a job by hand under Administration → E-mail still works.
maintenance.closed_text: The wiki is closed for maintenance. Please try again later.
maintenance.read_only_text: The wiki is read-only for maintenance: you can read everything, but nothing can be changed at the moment.
maintenance.bar_admin: As an administrator you can still change things.
consent.intro: Ask for consent to cookies and to the privacy policy, if your organisation needs it. The wiki itself only uses necessary storage (sign-in, protection against forged requests); services of others such as external videos are only loaded after consent.
consent.cookies_on_help: A banner asks which storage may be used beyond the necessary one: “Accept all”, “Only necessary” or a choice of categories. The choice is kept in the browser; people change it with the block “Cookie settings” or in their profile.
consent.cookies_required_help: The banner covers the page until a choice is made. “Only necessary” is a choice as well: consent to what is optional cannot be forced.
consent.text_help: Plain text; an empty line starts a new paragraph. Empty: a standard text.
consent.ask_again_help: For a changed text or policy: with the next version everybody is asked again; the proof keeps the earlier versions.
consent.privacy_on: Signed-in people accept the privacy policy
consent.privacy_on_help: After signing in, people see the privacy policy and can only accept it or sign out; the server enforces it for the browser (not for API keys). Administrators are asked as well but never locked out. Each acceptance is recorded with version and time.
consent.guests_help: Required for guests is kept in the browser: the wiki cannot recognise guests without storing something itself, so the server does not enforce it, and the plain HTML for search engines stays.
consent.privacy_text_user: Please read the privacy policy. To use the wiki, accept it; otherwise sign out and contact the people named in it.
consent.privacy_text_guest: Please read the privacy policy and accept it to use the wiki.
consent.privacy_notice: This wiki processes personal data as described in the privacy policy.
consent.cookies_text: This wiki uses storage in your browser that it needs to work (for example to keep you signed in). With your consent it may also use the following kinds. You can change your choice at any time under “Cookie settings”.
consent.cat_necessary_help: Signing in, protection against forged requests, your choices in this banner. Always on.
consent.cat_external_media_help: Videos and other content of services the administration allowed load without a second click; those services may then store and read data in your browser.
consent.profile_accepted: You accepted the privacy policy (version {version}) on {date}.
consent.profile_not_accepted: You have not accepted the privacy policy yet.
editor.width_help: Width: drag the edge, or use the arrow keys
editor.height_help: Minimum height: drag the lower edge or use the arrow keys
editor.size_bad_options: The options of this block cannot be read; change the size under Options.
placement.hidden_here_help: A level above shows these blocks; this category hides them. The boxes set where the hiding applies. Without a tick, the level above applies there again.
placement.unhidden: {block} is shown as in the level above again.
tasks.ticked: Task done. The page was saved.
tasks.reopened: Task open again. The page was saved.
tasks.title: My tasks
tasks.login: Sign in to see your tasks.
tasks.in_pages_help: Checklist items that name you with @name. Tick them here when they are done; the page is saved.
editor.task_help: A task item of a checklist. With a person or a date it appears in the report of tasks and under “My tasks” of the people.
editor.task_people_help: Search by name; several people are possible. One of them ticking is enough.
editor.task_need: Choose a person or a due date.
editor.task_desc: A task item with responsible people and a due date; it appears in the report of tasks and under “My tasks”.
editor.suggest_count_one: {count} block suggested. Arrow keys choose, Enter inserts, Escape closes.
editor.suggest_count_other: {count} blocks suggested. Arrow keys choose, Enter inserts, Escape closes.
bo.closable: Readers can close it (for example a notice bar; it comes back when its text changes)
bo.label: Name for screen readers
bo.label_help: Makes the block a region with this name, so screen reader users can find and skip it. At most 100 characters.
bo.scroll_height: Scrolls in itself from a height of
bo.sticky: Stays in view while its area scrolls (desktop only; only as the last block of its area and when it fits on the screen)
bo.border_sides.start: At the start of the line
bo.border_sides.end: At the end of the line
bo.border_sides.start_end: At the start and end of the line
bo.p.scroll_label: A block that scrolls in itself needs a name for screen readers.
bo.p.border_sides: Sides of the border need a border style.
bo.p.radius_corners: Rounded corners on some corners need a radius.
settings.form_allow_help: One address per line, only https:// and the server (for example https://news.example.com). The block Newsletter sign-up (external) may send the reader's e-mail address only to these services. Empty: no form sends anything outside the wiki.
media.redact_help: Mark the area on the picture (as for cropping), then choose how. Black fill and coarse blocks cannot be reversed; blurring can be partly, so it is not offered for this.
media.purge_help: Older versions still contain everything that was changed or made unreadable later. Deleting them removes their content from the wiki for good.
media.purge_confirm: Delete {n} older versions with their content? This cannot be undone.
media.purge_after_redact: The older versions still show what you made unreadable. Delete them now with their content? This cannot be undone.
media.purged_kept: {n} older versions deleted. {kept} of their files stay because other files or pages use the same content.
overview.open: Go to the overview of the administration
overview.help: The state of the wiki at a glance. Every tile leads to the matching page of the administration.
overview.auto_systemd: Installation with systemd: if the update timer is switched on (scripts/update.sh --enable-timer), it installs the newest version every Sunday. It does so between 03:30 and 04:30 (time of the server). The wiki cannot see whether it is switched on.
overview.auto_docker: Docker: the wiki does not update itself. Run the commands below in the directory of the installation.
overview.cmd_unknown: The wiki cannot tell how it was installed. Choose the command that matches your installation.
overview.cmd_fixed_tag: If the file .env sets a fixed version in EWIKI_IMAGE_TAG (for example 7.5), change it first.
overview.mfa_no_factors: No plugin for a second factor is switched on.
overview.plugins_isolation: All plugins are core plugins and run in the process of the wiki. Plugins as an own, isolated process (SDK) do not exist yet.
overview.timer_unreadable: The wiki could not read the state of the update helper (data/wiki/update-timer.json). Check the timer with scripts/update-docker.sh --status.
overview.timer_next: The update helper installs new versions daily. Next run: {date}.
overview.timer_next_window: The update helper installs new versions daily. Next run: {date}, up to {minutes} minutes later.
overview.timer_stale: The update helper last reported on {date}. Its timer may be switched off (scripts/update-docker.sh --status).
overview.timer_none: Docker: no automatic update set up. Set it up with scripts/update-docker.sh --enable-timer or run the commands below in the directory of the installation.
overview.timer_result_invalid_marker: invalid notice of an update, nothing changed
overview.timer_result_not_reached: version {version} not reached (fixed version in EWIKI_IMAGE_TAG?)
overview.timer_result_busy: another run was still going on
limit.core.notify.popups.help: How many unread pop-up notifications a person sees at most when a page loads; further ones follow on the next page loads.
popup.note: This message is in your notifications (bell) as well.
person.action_failed: That did not work. Please try again.
profile.email_hidden_help: Other people do not see your address on your profile page and in the menu on your name. Team pages are not affected: whoever builds a team page decides there.
settings.email_visibility: Who sees e-mail addresses of people
settings.email_visibility_help: On person pages, in the menu on names and in the people blocks. Team pages are not affected. Guests never see addresses here.
settings.email_vis_permission: Only with the permission “See e-mail addresses of people”
settings.email_hide_allowed: People may hide their own address
settings.email_hide_allowed_help: In their profile. A hidden address stays hidden for everybody else, administrators too.
settings.mention_display_help: Who may find a mentioned person sees the name with the menu. This sets what guests and all others see in place of @name.
perm.core.people.view_help: Open the page of a person and the menu on names (business card), for the people one may find.
perm.core.people.email_help: See the e-mail address on person pages when the settings show addresses only with this permission. Addresses people hide stay hidden.
limit.core.people.views_per_hour.help: Person pages and menus on names an account may open in one hour (administrators without limit). Protects the business cards and e-mail addresses from being collected in bulk.
settings.readability_help: While writing, the editor shows sentences and words that are too long. It never blocks saving and never changes the text.
settings.readability_mode_offered: Offered: each person can switch it on
settings.readability_mode_on: On for everybody: each person can switch it off
settings.readability_word_letters_help: Default 22. A hyphen splits a word. Allowed: 8 to 60.
profile.readability_help: While writing, the editor shows sentences and words that are too long. Code and addresses do not count.
readability.none: Readability: no long sentences or words.
readability.truncated: Only the start of the text was checked.
limit.core.ui.readability_kb: Text checked by the readability hint
limit.core.ui.readability_kb.help: The hint on long sentences and long words checks this much of a text while writing. The rest is not checked; the hint says so.
datepicker.title: Choose a date
datepicker.keys: Arrow keys: day and week. Page up and down: month. With Shift: year. Enter: choose. Escape: close.
choice.search_placeholder: At least {n} letters of the name
choice.keys_multiple: In the list: arrow keys move, Space chooses or removes, Shift+arrow chooses a range, Ctrl+A chooses all shown entries.
choice.keys_single: In the list: arrow keys move, Space chooses.
choice.more: Showing {n} of {total}. Type more to narrow the list.
settings.choice_checkboxes_help: Lists of groups, roles and similar with up to this many entries appear as checkboxes; longer lists as a list with a filter. 0 = 5, at most 50.
sitetpl.title: Templates
sitetpl.help: Website templates decide how the whole wiki looks. Which template applies is chosen here for the site and in the settings of a category.
sitetpl.overview_help: Each card shows where the positions of a template are. Choose a device to see the template on a tablet or a phone.
sitetpl.schema_none: This template has no schematic. Its positions: {list}
sitetpl.used_for_site: {name} is now the template of the website.
placement.choose_position: Choose a position in the schematic to see and change what is there.
sitetpl.positions_help: Each position of the template is a button in the schematic. A click shows what is there for the whole website. There you change the order and add or remove blocks. Choose the page shown and the device to see where the positions are there.
sitetpl.settings_help: The settings the template offers: colours, fonts, logos and more. Each field shows its default. The preview shows your changes at once; they count only after saving.
sitetpl.contrast_low: Contrast to {color} is only {ratio}:1; text needs at least 4.5:1.
sitetpl.link_invalid: A link starts with / or https://.
sitetpl.reset_all_confirm: Set all settings of {name} back to their defaults?
sitetpl.preview_help: Only you see the preview. Choose a device to see the website on a tablet or a phone.
